chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ahmad, from his father, and Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions one day: 'Do you think that if you were to gather what you have of clothing and utensils, then placed them atop one another, would you perceive them reaching the sky?' They replied, 'No, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'Shall I not inform you of something whose root is in the earth and its branches in the sky?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'One of you, upon completing the obligatory prayer, should say: Subhan Allah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar, thirty times. For indeed, their root is in the earth and their branches are in the sky. They prevent destruction, fire, drowning, falling in a well, consumption by wild beasts, death due to accidents, and the affliction that descends from the sky upon the servant on that day. They are the enduring good deeds.'

key_terms.التَّسْبِيحَاتُ الْأَرْبَعُ: The four glorifications: Subhan Allah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar
key_terms.الْأَصْلُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَ الْفَرْعُ فِي: Root in the earth and branches in the sky, indicating spiritual ascent and connection

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and protective benefit of reciting Tasbihat al-Arba' after prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) illustrates the metaphysical ascent of the Tasbihat al-Arba' by describing their 'root in the earth and branch in the sky,' a concept reflecting the Shia understanding of dhikr as a bridge between the material and spiritual realms. This specific recitation of thirty times after obligatory prayers is highlighted not only for its protective power against diverse calamities but also as the quintessential 'enduring good deeds' (al-baqiyat al-salihat) that continue to benefit the believer beyond their immediate performance.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 4. And with this chain of narration from Ahmad, from his father, and Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (AS), who said: "

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (sw) said to his companions one day, 'Do you think that if you were to gather what you have of clothing and utensils, then placed them atop one another, would you perceive them reaching the sky?' They replied, 'No, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'Shall I not inform you of something whose root is in the earth and its branches in the sky?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'One of you, upon completing the obligatory prayer, should say: Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), Alhamdulillah (Praise be to Allah), La ilaha illallah (There is no god but Allah), Allahu Akbar (Allah is Greater than what can be described); thirty times. For indeed, their root is in the earth and their branches are in the sky. They prevent destruction, fire, drowning, falling in a well, consumption by wild beasts, death due to accidents, and the affliction that descends from the sky upon the servant on that day. They are the enduring good deeds.'"
